questions.q: Two open organ pipes of lengths $60 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $90 \mathrm{~cm}$ resonate at $6^{\text {th }}$ and $5^{\text {th }}$ harmonics respectively. The difference of frequencies for the given modes is _______ $\mathrm{Hz}$. (Velocity of sound in air $=333 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ )
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: The equation of wave is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>160</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math> are in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>s</mi></math>. The speed of the wave is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equation of the wave is 

Y=10-2sin2π(160t-0.5x+π4)

The velocity of a wave is given by v=ωk   ...(i).

A wave equation is given by 

Y=Asinωt-kx+ϕ

Using equation (i),

v=2π×1602π×0.5=320 m s-1

⇒v=320×185

⇒v=1152 km h-1

questions.q: Two travelling waves of equal amplitudes and equal frequencies move in opposite directions along a string. They interfere to produce a stationary wave whose equation is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>10</mn><mi>cos</mi><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi><mi>sin</mi><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mi>cm</mi></math>. The amplitude of the particle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position, for that

sin2πtT=1

Therefore, A=10cos43π=10×12= 5 cm

questions.q: Two waves are simultaneously passing through a string and their equations are : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mi>k</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mi>k</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Given amplitudes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>,  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and wave number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>28</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The amplitude of resulting wave will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Δϕ=kx0=2πλx0=2π×3.5  λ=2πk=1

=2π×3510=7π

AR=122+52+2×12×5×cos(7π)=(12-5)2=7 mm

questions.q: A tuning fork resonates with a sonometer wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> stretched with a tension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> When the tension in the wire is changed to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the same tuning fork produces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn></math> beats per second with it. The frequency of the tuning fork is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Frequency of sonometer wire is given by, f=12 LTμ

Therefore, f1=126μ f2=1254μ

Hence, f1f2=13 

Also it is given that, f2-f1=12

So, f1=6 Hz.

questions.q: The fundamental frequency of vibration of a string between two rigid support is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The mass of the string is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>18</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and its linear mass density is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The speed of the transverse waves so produced in the string is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The fundamental frequency is f=50 Hz.

The length of the string is l=λ2

Linear mass density is μ=ml=20 g m-1

Using v=fλ

v2l=50

⇒v=100×l=100×1820=90 m s-1

The node closest to the origin in the region <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> will be at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced><mrow><mtext>in</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>

questions.solution:
At Node,
y=0

⇒cos1.57xsin78.5t=0

questions.q: In an experiment to determine the velocity of sound in air at room temperature using a resonance tube, the first resonance is observed when the air column has a length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> for a tuning fork of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is used. The velocity of the sound at room temperature is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>336</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The third resonance is observed when the air column has a length of _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Wavelength of wave ⇒λ=vf=336400=84 cm

At first resonance

λ4=l+e⇒844=20+e, where, e is end correction.

⇒e=1
So third resonance length

5λ4=l2+e

521=l2+1

l2=104 cm

questions.q: The distance between two consecutive points with phase difference of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> in a wave of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The velocity with which wave is travelling is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Distance between two consecutive points 60° out of phase is given by Δx=λ2πΔϕ

Putting the values, we have

6=λ2ππ3

⇒λ=36 m

Now, velocity of wave is v=fλ=(500 Hz)(36 m)

=18000 m s-1=18 km s-1

questions.q: A wire having a linear mass density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>900</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The wire resonates at a frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The next higher frequency at which the same wire resonates is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>550</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The length of the wire is ___________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
fn=nv2ℓ=500
fn+1=(n+1)v2ℓ=550
n+1n=1110
Thus, n=10
Thus, ℓ=nv2fnv=Tμ
=102×500×9009×10-4=10 m

questions.q: The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-direction is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> at time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>s</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math>

questions.solution:
At t=0,y=11+x2
At time t=t,y=11+(x-vt)2
At t=1,y=11+(x-v)2 …(i)
At t=1,y=11+(x-2)2 …(ii)
Comparing (i) and (ii)
v=2 m s-1

questions.q: A closed and an open organ pipe have same lengths. If the ratio of frequencies of their seventh overtones is $\left(\frac{a-1}{a}\right)$ then the value of $\mathrm{a}$ is ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For closed organ pipe
$\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}=(2 \mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}=\frac{15 \mathrm{v}}{4 \ell}$
For open organ pipe
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}=(\mathrm{n}+1) \frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \ell}=\frac{8 \mathrm{v}}{2 \ell} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{c}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{o}}}=\frac{15}{16}=\frac{\mathrm{a}-1}{\mathrm{a}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=16\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>, stretched between rigid supports, has it's <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>th</mi><mo> </mo></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi>th</mi></msup></math> harmonics at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>450</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>, respectively. If tension in the string is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2700</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, it's linear mass density is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Frequency of nth harmonic is nv2l=400⇒nv0.6=400   ...1 

And frequency of n+1th harmonic is n+1v2l=450⇒n+1v0.6=450    ...2, here, v is speed of wave on string. 

From equation 1, we have

n=400×0.6v

Putting in equation 2, 

⇒0.6×400v+1v0.6=450

⇒400+v0.6=450

⇒v=30 m s-1

Speed of wave on string is stated as v=Tμ=30, here, μ is linear mass density.

So, μ=Tv2=2700900⇒μ=3 kg m-1

questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave passing through a string of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The area of cross-section of the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and its Young's modulus is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The extension of the wire over its natural length due to its tension will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The wave speed in string is given by vw=Tμ, where, T is tension and μ=ml is linear mass density.

Putting the values, we have

⇒60=T10×10-3×0.5

⇒T=602×10-20.5=72 N

The Young's modulus is given by Y=FlA∆l, here, A is area.

From above the extension of the wire is Δl=TlAY=72×0.52×10-6×1.2×1011=72×524×10-5=15×10-5 m.

Hence, the value of x=15.

questions.q: A guitar string of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>90</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> vibrates with a fundamental frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The length of the string producing a fundamental of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency produced in a vibrating string is given by

f0=v2L   ...1

For the first case, it can be written that

120=v2(90)    ...2

Similarly, for the second case, it can be written that

180=v2(L)    ...3

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) and solve to obtain the required length of the string.

180120=v2Lv290= 90L⇒L= 90×120180=60

questions.q: In a closed organ pipe, the frequency of fundamental note is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. A certain amount of water is now poured in the organ pipe so that the fundamental frequency is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>110</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. If the organ pipe has a cross-sectional area of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the amount of water poured in the organ tube is ________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>. (Take speed of sound in air is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>330</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency for closed organ pipe in the first part:

V4l1=30⇒l1=114 m

Similarly, for second part:

V4l2=110⇒l2=34 m

Therefore, change in length Δl=2 m

Change in volume =AΔl=400 cm3

M=400 g;∵ρ=1 g cm-3

questions.q: For a certain organ pipe, the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of 1:3:5 respectively. If the frequency of fifth harmonic is 405 Hz and the speed of sound in air is 324 m s–1 the length of the organ pipe is _____ m.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given,

f5=405 Hz.

As the first three resonance frequencies are in the ratio of 1:3:5, therefore it must be a closed organ pipe.

The frequency formula in a closed organ pipe is given by f=nv4l. So,

5v4I=405 Hz

⇒I=405×45×324=1 m

questions.q: In an experiment with sonometer when a mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>180</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is attached to the string, it vibrates with fundamental frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. When a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is attached, the string vibrates with fundamental frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the fundamental frequency in a stretched string is given by

f=12LTμ   ...1

For the first mass, it can be written that

f1=12Lm1gμ   ...2

And, for the second mass, it can be written that

f2=12Lm2gμ   ...3

Divide equation (3) by equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required mass.

f2f1=12Lm2gμ12Lm1gμ= m2m1⇒m1m2=f1f22⇒m2=m1f2f12   ...4

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (4) to calculate the required mass.

m2=180 g×50 Hz30 Hz2= 500 g

questions.q: A tuning fork is vibrating at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The length of the shortest closed organ pipe that will resonate with the tuning fork will be _____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>. (Take speed of sound in air as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>340</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For closed organ pipe

f=(2n+1)v4l

for minimum length, n=0

f0=v4l

⇒l=v4f0

questions.q: A wire of density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two clamps <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> apart. The extension developed in the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>10</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the fundamental frequency of vibration in the wire will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hz</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the relation of Young's modulus,

 TA=YΔLL  
⇒T=YΔLL×A

The linear mass density is  μ=mL.

So,
Tμ=YΔLALmL=Y(ΔL)×LAL(m)=YΔLL×1ρ

Substituting the values,
Tμ=8×1010×3.2×10-40.5×18×103=6.4×103
⇒Tμ=64×102

The fundamental frequency is given by f=12LTμ.
⇒Tμ=8×10=80 m s-1
Therefore,

f=801=80 Hz
